title: Your First Mortgage Payment Barely Touches The Loan. Here's Why.
description:
Educational purposes only. Not financial advice.

Mortgages use amortization schedules that front-load interest: in the early years, the majority of each fixed payment covers interest on the full remaining balance, with only a small slice reducing principal. Over time that ratio flips, and later payments knock down principal much faster. It's a structural feature of how the loan is repaid, not a hidden fee.
